author: Frances Jenkins Olcott (compiler); stories by various authors, many adapted by her
title: Good Stories for Great Holidays
edition: Project Gutenberg 359 plain-text transcription (produced by Mike Lough) of Frances Jenkins Olcott, Good Stories for Great Holidays, Arranged for Story-Telling and Reading Aloud and for the Children's Own Reading (Boston and New York: Houghton Mifflin Company, The Riverside Press Cambridge; copyright 1914, published October 1914); the transcription does not name its print exemplar. The library text holds Olcott's preface “To the Story-Teller” and every story in printed order under its holiday section title, with its printed byline or subtitle and the source footnotes as the transcription places them (after the byline, numbered as the transcription numbers them). Omitted: the title leaves, contents, list of illustrations, the illustrations and captions, the acknowledgments page (not in the transcription), the closing reference lists for story-telling and collateral reading, and the index. The transcription sets the printed italics in capital letters; outside the collated stories they are kept as it gives them. Its straight apostrophes, curly double quotation marks and double-hyphen dashes are retained; paragraph wrapping is joined with single spaces; verse lines are kept as stanza lines with indentation dropped, a verse line the transcription wraps being rejoined. On 2026-11-18 ten stories read by Grade 1 and Grade 2 calendar readings (blocks 11–31, 117–151, 386–435, 752–771, 815–845, 1180–1189, 1430–1442, 1507–1519 and 1627–1640: “The Fairy's New Year Gift”, “The Mail-Coach Passengers”, “A Lesson of Faith”, “Betsy Ross and the Flag”, “The Star-Spangled Banner”, “Two Hero-Stories of the Civil War”, “Columbus and the Egg”, “The King of the Cats”, “The First Harvest-Home in Plymouth” and “The Spirit of the Corn”, each with its title, byline and footnote) were collated in full against the 1914 Houghton Mifflin printing (https://archive.org/details/goodstoriesforgr00olco, New York Public Library copy; copyright page at scan leaf 12), word by word against its OCR text (https://archive.org/download/goodstoriesforgr00olco/goodstoriesforgr00olco_djvu.txt) with every difference decided on its page images (pages 1–3, 18–24, 71–77, 137–141, 148–152, 213–214, 256–258, 269–271 and 290–292): their words agree except for six transcription errors corrected to the printing (“book?” to “book,”, “bore” to “born”, “were-empty” to “were empty”, the footnote's “1903” to “1905”, Bradford's “ye goodly” to the printed “yt goodly”, and the comma restored in “from the earth, and”) and “JR” to “JR.” in a byline; in these stories every word the transcription sets in capitals for the printed italics was checked on the page and restored as _italics_, and the italic book title in footnote 8 is marked the same way. The printing's spaced contractions (“I 'd”) are given closed, as the transcription gives them.

rights.basis: Published in the United States in 1914 by Houghton Mifflin Company (copyright 1914 by Frances Jenkins Olcott), before 1931, so its US copyright term has expired by 2026; every story it reprints or adapts appeared in or before this 1914 edition. Illustrations and their captions are excluded.

acquisition.method: Downloaded Project Gutenberg plain text pg359.txt (UTF-8, CRLF) from the aleph.pglaf.org mirror of the Gutenberg cache and converted with a scratch script: line ends normalized; the text taken from “TO THE STORY-TELLER” up to “CONTENTS”, then from the first story, “THE FAIRY'S NEW YEAR GIFT”, up to “THE END”, so that the Project Gutenberg header, producer credit, title leaf, contents, half-title, the closing “THE END”, the reference lists and the Gutenberg footer and licence are left out. Blocks are the transcription's blank-line-separated paragraphs. A single-line capitalized block is a level-1 heading when it is one of the sixteen holiday section titles (the dates printed under them stay paragraphs), a level-3 heading when it is a numbered or titled part within a story (“I. THE CHERRY TREE”, “THE ENCHANTED PALACE”, “II”), a paragraph when it is a byline or subtitle (“BY …”, “(ADAPTED)”, “AN IROQUOIS LEGEND”, “AFTER CELIA THAXTER” and the like, and the lettering “GEORGE WASHINGTON” inside a story), and otherwise a level-2 story heading. A block whose first line is indented three or more spaces is a stanza: one line per transcription line, indentation dropped and runs of spaces folded, a line indented only one or two spaces joined to the line before it as the transcription's wrap. Other blocks are paragraphs with lines joined by single spaces. “[Footnote: 9: …]” is normalized to “[Footnote 9: …]”.
